# jumpcloud_service_account (Resource)

Manages a service account, which calls the JumpCloud admin API with OAuth 2.0 client credentials instead of an admin's API key. Exchange `client_id` and `client_secret` for a token at `https://admin-oauth.id.jumpcloud.com/oauth2/token` with `grant_type=client_credentials` and `scope=api`, then call the API with `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. The account can do what its admin role allows. See [Service Account for APIs](https://jumpcloud.com/support/service-account-for-apis).

JumpCloud cannot change a service account, so changing any argument replaces it, with a new client ID and secret. Creating one needs an API key whose admin has the Billing role, and an organization can have at most 40.

~> JumpCloud returns the client secret only when the account is created, so `client_secret` is stored in the Terraform state and is empty after an import. Use a state backend that encrypts its data. The secret stops working at `expires_at`; replace the account before then.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "jumpcloud_role" "read_only" {
  name = "Read Only"
}

resource "jumpcloud_service_account" "sa_example" {
  name                 = "sa-example"
  role_id              = data.jumpcloud_role.read_only.id
  secret_lifetime_days = 365
}

# Hand the credentials to the application without them leaving Terraform.
resource "aws_secretsmanager_secret_version" "jumpcloud" {
  secret_id = aws_secretsmanager_secret.jumpcloud.id
  secret_string = jsonencode({
    client_id     = jumpcloud_service_account.sa_example.client_id
    client_secret = jumpcloud_service_account.sa_example.client_secret
  })
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Name shown in the admin console. Changing it replaces the account.
- `role_id` (String) ID of the admin role that decides what the account can do, such as one from `jumpcloud_role`. Changing it replaces the account.

### Optional

- `secret_lifetime_days` (Number) Days until the client secret expires: `30`, `60`, `90`, or `365`. Defaults to `365`. Changing it replaces the account.

### Read-Only

- `client_id` (String) OAuth client ID.
- `client_secret` (String, Sensitive) OAuth client secret. Empty after an import.
- `expires_at` (String) When the client secret expires, in RFC 3339 format.
- `id` (String) Service account ID.
- `status` (String) State of the client secret: `ACTIVE`, `EXPIRING` when it expires soon, or `EXPIRED`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by service account ID. JumpCloud never returns the secret again, so
# client_secret is empty after an import; replace the account to get a new one.
terraform import jumpcloud_service_account.sa_example 6ac6b310f1aac9c461f1da73
```
